title: Joshua J. Taylor
text:
I am a research associate at the Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Sciences at the University of Texas at Austin. I am also affiliated with CosmicAI, the NSF–Simons AI Institute for Cosmic Origins.
My research is in unsupervised learning of scientific data that are large, high-dimensional, and noisy, where no labels exist to guide scientific analysis. I am drawn to this problem because unsupervised learning is the most direct route to discovery. It can surface populations and physical regimes that no one thought to look for, but also brings its own assumptions about what counts as structure. My own methods, built on prototype learning, learned connectivity graphs, and low-dimensional embeddings, are designed to be rooted in as much data evidence as possible.
I work primarily inside astronomy, specifically parsing the spectral cubes, infrared surveys, and simulations of star-formation astrophysics to learn how gas in molecular clouds assembles into stars. My long-term goal is a general paradigm for physics-informed unsupervised learning.

title: Research
text: Modern scientific instruments and simulations produce data that are large, high-dimensional, and noisy. Much of what a scientist wants from such data depends on knowing what they contain, namely which populations or physical regimes are present and what those imply about physics. When no labels exist, that question falls to unsupervised learning, which in turn hands an analyst every degree of freedom a label would otherwise have fixed, such as data resolutions, neighborhood sizes, cluster counts, and model forms. My work builds methods that let the data make those choices.

title: Research
section: Methods that set their own parameters
text:
Methods that set their own parameters
I work with neural prototype learning, which compresses a large data set into a small set of representative observations that remain in the units of the data, and with the connectivity graph that can be inferred from those prototypes. Together they act as a meta-learned product that supplies the degrees of freedom an analyst would otherwise have to guess. Along this line I have set vector quantizer resolution from density-estimation efficiency, replaced the manual perplexity of t-SNE with learned manifold connectivity, built a Self-Organizing UMAP in which prototypes and their embedding learn from each other, given graph sparsification a Bayesian stopping rule, and combined all of it in MPEC, a multiview prototype embedding and clustering method for spectral cubes. The Quantized Infinitesimal Jackknife extends the same machinery to uncertainty quantification for prototype-based statistics.

title: Research
text:
Science from those methods
In simulations of star-forming clouds, prototype embeddings organized thousands of dense gas cores into three evolutionary phases with no knowledge of their fates, and mapping observed cores into the same space predicted that a substantial fraction of cataloged starless cores will never form stars. In the Green Bank Ammonia Survey, MPEC found spatially coherent gas structures from spectral similarity alone, raised the signal-to-noise of faint emission by pooling, and revealed velocity offsets between molecular species that signal gas falling onto the Orion A filament. In the Spitzer Extended Solar Neighborhood Archive, I am building a fully Bayesian census of young stars in which selection effects and missing photometry are modeled rather than cleaned away.

title: Research
text:
Where this is going
Physics-informed supervised learning now has a settled vocabulary for where physics enters a model. Its unsupervised counterpart does not exist yet. My long-term program is to build it: methods in which physical constraints shape how structure is discovered without foreclosing the discovery of regimes that existing models do not anticipate, with the statistical accounting to say how much of a result the physics decided.

title: Software
text:
Open-source Python packages behind the methods, each with documentation and tutorials.
soumap · GitHub
Self-Organizing UMAP: a hybrid SOM/UMAP algorithm that jointly learns data prototypes and their low-dimensional embedding, with multiview clustering (MPEC).
vqlp · GitHub
Vector quantization under arbitrary Lp metrics, with recall quantities: prototype assignments, quantization error, receptive fields, and the connectivity graph.
gtsom · GitHub
General-topology Self-Organizing Maps: SOM training on arbitrary output-space geometries.
qij
The Quantized Infinitesimal Jackknife: variance for estimators without a closed-form influence function.
NeuralVQ · GitHub
Earlier neural vector quantization tools, kept for reproducibility of published results.
